meeting-stranger.setting: You meet someone in the plaza. She smiles and waves.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Hi! My name is María. What's your name?

options.feedback: ¡Perfecto! That's the natural way to introduce yourself.
'Buenas noches' means 'good night' — she asked your name.
That means 'thanks, goodbye' — she's just meeting you!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Nice to meet you. Where are you from?

options.feedback: ¡Bien! 'Soy de + place' is how you say where you're from.
Use 'soy de' (I am from) — not 'tengo' (I have).
Origin uses 'ser' not 'estar' — soy de…

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Great! Welcome. See you later.

asking-directions-basic.setting: You see a friendly man at the plaza. He looks ready to chat.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Hello! How are you today?

options.feedback: ¡Excelente! Returning the question is polite.
Feelings use 'estar' — 'estoy bien', not 'soy bien'.
'Tengo' = I have. For feelings use 'estoy'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Estoy muy contento. Hace sol hoy.
lines.translation: I'm very happy. It's sunny today.

options.feedback: ¡Bien! Great way to continue weather chat.
He just said it's sunny — try agreeing with the nice day.
Don't end the conversation yet — he just made small talk!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Have a good day. Goodbye!

family-talk.setting: You're at a café with Ana, who shows you a family photo.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mira, esta es mi familia. Tengo dos hermanos.
lines.translation: Look, this is my family. I have two brothers.

options.feedback: ¡Perfecto! A natural follow-up question.
That's a strange response — try asking about her family.
Don't say goodbye! Engage with her family story.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Pedro y Luis. Mi madre se llama Sofía. ¿Y tu familia?
lines.translation: Pedro and Luis. My mother is Sofía. And your family?

options.text: Tengo una hermana. Mi madre se llama Linda.
options.feedback: ¡Genial! Mirroring her structure is great.
Reorder: 'Tengo tres hermanas' = I have three sisters.
Use 'se llama' (is named): 'Mi madre se llama Linda.'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: What a lovely family! Thanks for sharing.

ordering-food.setting: You're at a food stand. The vendor smiles.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Welcome! What do you want to eat today?

options.text: Quiero pollo con arroz, por favor.
options.feedback: ¡Muy bien! Polite and clear.
'Tengo' means 'I have' — use 'quiero' (I want) to order.
'Soy pollo' means 'I am chicken' — use 'quiero'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Perfect. Do you want a drink too?

options.feedback: ¡Bien! Simple and polite.
Just say 'No, gracias' or 'Sí, agua por favor.'
Use 'quiero agua' (I want water).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: That's eight euros total.

options.feedback: ¡Perfecto! Polite handover.
He told you the price — just pay or confirm.
Just hand over the money: 'Aquí tienes.'

shopping-clothes.setting: You're at a clothing stall in the market.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Hello, do you need help?

options.feedback: ¡Bien! Specific and polite.
'Soy azul' = 'I am blue.' Use 'busco' (I'm looking for).
Don't lead with that! Just say what you're looking for.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Tenemos camisas azules grandes y pequeñas. ¿Cuál quieres?
lines.translation: We have big and small blue shirts. Which do you want?

options.feedback: ¡Excelente! Clear choice.
Use 'quiero' to order, not 'tengo' (I have).
Don't insult the merchandise! Pick a size.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: It costs twenty euros.

options.feedback: ¡Perfecto! Standard purchase.
It's actually a fair price — try negotiating politely or accepting.
That's not how it works! Just say yes or counter politely.

weather-chat.setting: Diego is sitting on a bench, watching the sky.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: It's really hot today, isn't it?

options.feedback: ¡Bien! Adding to his observation.
Word order: 'Tengo mucho calor' — but 'Sí, hace mucho calor' fits the chat.
It's hot, not snowing! 'Hace sol' fits.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: What are you going to do today?

options.text: Voy a la playa esta tarde.
options.feedback: ¡Genial! Future plan with 'voy a + place'.
Just one verb: 'Voy a la playa.'
'Tengo' = I have. Use 'voy a' for plans.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: How nice! Enjoy your day.

asking-directions-city.setting: You're lost downtown. You stop a kind-looking woman.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Do you need help?

options.feedback: ¡Bien! Direct and polite.
Use 'dónde está' (where is) to ask for a place.
Use 'está lejos' (it's far) — but better to ask 'dónde está…'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Sigue recto dos calles, después a la derecha.
lines.translation: Go straight two streets, then turn right.

options.text: Recto y a la derecha. Gracias.
options.feedback: ¡Perfecto! Confirming shows you understood.
She said RIGHT, not left — derecha.
Try repeating what you understood — that helps.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: It's near the traffic light. Good luck!

daily-routine.setting: Your friend Miguel asks about your morning over coffee.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: What time do you usually wake up?

options.feedback: ¡Bien! Reflexive verb correctly used.
Reflexive: 'me levanto' — I get myself up.
'Ducharse' = to shower. He asked when you get up.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Yo me levanto a las seis. Después desayuno y trabajo.
lines.translation: I get up at six. Then I have breakfast and work.

options.text: ¡Qué temprano! Yo desayuno y luego trabajo también.
options.feedback: ¡Perfecto! Sharing your routine in return.
Try sharing your routine — that's what he's looking for.
Words are out of order. Try a complete sentence.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Buena rutina. ¡Que tengas un buen día!
lines.translation: Good routine. Have a great day!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Hi! What are you doing now?

options.feedback: ¡Bien! Casual and inviting.
Just say 'nada' (nothing) or 'No mucho.'
Try 'No hago nada' (I'm not doing anything) instead.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Do you want to go to the movies tonight?

options.feedback: ¡Perfecto! Agreeing and getting details.
Use 'estoy ocupado' for being busy. But say yes — it's a fun plan!
Mixed tenses. Try: 'Sí, vamos a las ocho.'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: At eight. See you later!

hotel-checkin.setting: You arrive at the hotel reception, suitcase in hand.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: Good afternoon, do you have a reservation?

options.text: Sí, tengo una reserva a nombre de Alex.
options.feedback: ¡Excelente! Very natural check-in line.
Use 'tengo una reserva' (I have a reservation).
Just confirm you have one — 'Sí, tengo reserva.'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Aquí tiene su llave. Habitación 302, segundo piso.
lines.translation: Here's your key. Room 302, second floor.

options.feedback: ¡Bien! Practical follow-up.
Try a complete reply: 'Gracias' is enough or ask a question.
Funny but no — 'gracias' is what you want.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Sí, a la derecha. ¡Que tenga buena estancia!
lines.translation: Yes, to the right. Have a good stay!

future-plans.setting: Roberto asks about your future at a party.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.translation: What will you do next year?

options.feedback: ¡Genial! Future tense used correctly.
'Ayer' is yesterday — use future: 'Iré' or 'Voy a ir'.
'Fui' is past. Use 'iré' (I will go) for the future.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: ¡Qué interesante! Deberías visitar Sevilla. Es muy bonita.
lines.translation: How interesting! You should visit Seville. It's very pretty.

options.feedback: ¡Perfecto! Accepting advice graciously.
He's giving YOU advice — accept or thank him.
Try 'Quiero visitarla' (I want to visit it).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Vas a tener una experiencia genial.
lines.translation: You'll have a great experience.

debate-topic.setting: You're at a dinner party. Elena starts a friendly debate.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Creo que es mejor vivir en la ciudad que en el campo.
lines.translation: I think living in the city is better than in the country.

options.text: No estoy de acuerdo. El campo es más tranquilo.
options.feedback: ¡Excelente! Polite disagreement with reason.
Try a full sentence: 'Estoy de acuerdo' or 'No estoy de acuerdo.'
Try expressing your opinion clearly.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Pero la ciudad tiene más oportunidades.
lines.translation: But the city has more opportunities.

options.text: Sin embargo, el campo es más sano.
options.feedback: ¡Genial! Using 'sin embargo' to counter is sophisticated.
Try: 'Es verdad, pero…' or 'Sin embargo…'
Don't leave the conversation! Counter her point.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Buenos puntos. En conclusión, depende de la persona.
lines.translation: Good points. In conclusion, it depends on the person.
